A.explanation: 120 m would correspond to dividing by about 0.83, not by the given $0.800$ factor for the resistive force.

B.explanation: With the same initial kinetic energy, $F \times 100 = 0.800F \times d$, so $d = 100/0.800 = 125 \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: 156 m results from multiplying $125$ by $1.25$ again, applying the $1/0.800$ factor twice instead of once.

D.explanation: 250 m would require the resistive force to halve to $0.500F$, not to decrease only to $0.800F$.

hints: Notice both runs start with the same car at the same speed, so the initial kinetic energy to be removed is identical.
Recall work done by a constant resistive force is $W = Fd$, and this work removes all the initial kinetic energy to bring the car to rest.
Set $F \times 100 \text{ m} = 0.800F \times d$ and solve for the new stopping distance $d$.
walkthrough: The car has the same mass and same initial speed in both cases, so its initial kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is the same.
When the engine is off, the resistive force does negative work $W = Fd$ to reduce this $E_k$ to zero, so $F \times d = E_k$.
Second case with force $0.800F$ and unknown distance $d_2$: $0.800F \times d_2 = E_k$.
Equate the two expressions for $E_k$: $0.800F \times d_2 = F \times 100 \text{ m}$.
Cancel $F$: $d_2 = 100/0.800 = 125 \text{ m}$, with unit $\text{m}$ as expected for distance. This is option B.
